delta: House at 88 against a core model at 81 and markets at 94.
mechanisms: The chamber model's 3-point shared swing plus coarse ratings widen the distribution past what the generic lead supports | The markets price the generic ballot at D+9.5 and give almost nothing to a miss toward Republicans | Redistricting is worth more than the raters' 5 flips to Republicans show

conclusion: 88. The downside case is a Republican hold at 218 to 222 and needs a miss of 5 or more, which no midterm in the modern polling record has produced.
falsifier: A final national House vote under D+4 with Republicans at 218 or more.

mechanisms: Stevens's suburban voters follow her to Rogers in numbers that matter, 2 points or more | The endorsement is an elite event that changes prices and not votes, as most late endorsements do | Michigan's polls were already 1 to 2 points too Democratic and the endorsement only confirms a race closer than +5

conclusion: Take 1.5 for the endorsement and 1.5 for the state's net polling history. +5.4 becomes about +2.5. 70. This is the one race in the run where today's news moved a number, and the cap on judgment in the core model will keep it from moving the board by more than 3 points of margin.
falsifier: El-Sayed winning by 5 or more says the endorsement was priced and worth nothing. Rogers winning says it was worth more than 2.

delta: South Carolina Senate at 13 and the margin at Graham +6, against four nonpartisan polls averaging Graham +2.3 and markets at 25.5.
mechanisms: The 2020 South Carolina miss of 6.5 toward the Democrat recurs because the same pollsters are measuring the same electorate | The three nonpartisan likely-voter polls within 4 points are right and the race is a genuine toss-up | The doubled early turnout is new voters the county mix cannot see
evidence: Early voting closed at 1.87 times 2022's pace with the Harris counties at 24.45 percent of ballots against 24.93 in 2022 and the geography estimate within 0.7 of 2022. The pre-registered test for the flip trigger was not met. The Black share of mail ballots is 27.1 against 24.2 at 2022's close, the one composition figure that leans the other way.
conclusion: 13 and Graham by 6. The electorate that has voted looks like 2022, when Scott won by 26 and Graham in 2020 by 10 after polls had him near even.
falsifier: Andrews within 3 says the county mix was the wrong lens. Graham by 10 or more says the polls repeated 2020.

conclusion: The opposite reading is that this run has repeated the lock's mistake in the other direction: it discounts red-state polls on three cycles of history, two of them with Trump on the ballot, while the actual ballots in hand say the opposite. North Carolina's Republicans have not shown up early at their 2022 or 2024 rates. Every state with party registration has Democrats above their share of the rolls. The specials ran D+10 to 13 all year and did not fade. Virginia and New Jersey beat their polls toward Democrats by 5 and 10 last November with the same pollsters and the same weighting. If the polls are simply right, Brown wins by 3, Talarico by 2, Jackson by 3, Peltola by 2, and the Senate is 52 to 48 with this run 20 points too low. The second counter-case is the one Jake holds: the polls are 4 or more too Democratic everywhere, Republicans hold Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Alaska, Maine and Kansas, Michigan falls, and the Senate is 52 to 48 the other way. This run gives that about 4 percent and the first counter-case about 25. To believe Republicans hold the House I would need to see: a final national House vote under D+4, Republicans ahead in the early-counting Florida and Georgia House seats by 9 pm ET, Democrats failing to flip PA-07, PA-08 and NY-17, and a Republican share of the North Carolina Election Day vote above 45 percent.

conclusion: 88. The downside case is a Republican hold at 218 to 222 and needs a miss of 5 or more, which no midterm in the modern polling record has produced.
falsifier: A final national House vote under D+4 with Republicans at 218 or more.

delta: Michigan Senate from 72 to 70, and the drop since this morning is 8 points, the largest one-day move of the run.
mechanisms: Stevens's suburban voters follow her to Rogers in numbers that matter, 2 points or more | The endorsement is an elite event that changes prices and not votes, as most late endorsements do | Michigan's polls were already 1 to 2 points too Democratic and the endorsement only confirms a race closer than +5
evidence: No poll will field after the endorsement. Polymarket fell 7.5 points in two hours and recovered 3. The nonpartisan average before it was +5.4 across seven polls including a YouGov at +4 on Oct 29. falsifier: El-Sayed winning by 5 or more says the endorsement was priced and worth nothing. Rogers winning says it was worth more than 2.

delta: South Carolina Senate at 13 and the margin at Graham +6, against four nonpartisan polls averaging Graham +2.3 and markets at 25.5.
mechanisms: The 2020 South Carolina miss of 6.5 toward the Democrat recurs because the same pollsters are measuring the same electorate | The three nonpartisan likely-voter polls within 4 points are right and the race is a genuine toss-up | The doubled early turnout is new voters the county mix cannot see
evidence: Early voting closed at 1.87 times 2022's pace with the Harris counties at 24.45 percent of ballots against 24.93 in 2022 and the geography estimate within 0.7 of 2022.
